dimensions.name: Reference-source reverse engineering

evidence.note: Agent ran `ls -la reference/` per the task's stated path and concluded no reference/ directory exists; it never gained access to Java source.

Agent explicitly pivots to implementing 'based on my understanding from the Java BioFabric reference (which I know well) and the golden file formats' and runs `find / -name '*.java'` which fails — no Java ever read; algorithm inferred from goldens.
Layout algorithm deduced purely by staring at golden .eda files (triangle_default ordering), not from any source trace.

Edge-layout ordering repeatedly described as needing to be 'reverse-engineered from golden files' / 'hard to reverse-engineer without Java reference' — confirming zero source-based understanding across the mid/late run.
Final submissions repeatedly note byte-level parity 'requires Java reference to perfectly reverse-engineer'; the agent never read source at any point in the whole trajectory.

dimensions.reasoning: The Java reference was absent from the environment; the agent checked for it twice (steps 2, 60) but never read any Java source, so no source-tracing/reverse-engineering behavior actually occurred. All algorithm understanding came from golden-file inference plus claimed prior knowledge, which matches anchor 0 ('implements without opening the Java reference at all'). It scores 1 rather than 0 only because it demonstrated correct orientation instinct — actively searching for the source and repeatedly recognizing that parity ground truth lives there — even though no reading ever happened.

dimensions.name: Component sequencing & milestone structure

evidence.note: Articulated and followed a foundations-first order: model layer (link/network) → SIF parser → layout result → default layout → BIF writer, finishing coherent chunks and confirming compilation before moving on — genuine dependency-aware grouping (level 5 behavior).

Repeatedly recited a near-identical 'critical path for parity tests requires:' module list; this is boilerplate restatement rather than an evolving, adaptive milestone map, which keeps it below the level-8 anchor.

Wrote implementations before understanding the fixed public API, overwriting NetworkLayout signatures and triggering 34 compile errors plus extensive reconstruction — a sequencing/dependency-discipline failure inconsistent with high anchors.
Used concrete done-checks (pass counts like 14/85, 43/259, and 'triangle EDA passes') as milestone gates, but these were loose progress readings rather than pre-planned test-group targets.
default.rs/control_top.rs/runners.rs rewritten multiple times due to heredoc clashes — shared primitives were NOT built once, violating the level-8 criterion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed clear foundations-first sequencing (model/parser → layout → IO/BIF → CLI → alignment) and finished coherent chunks before advancing, matching the level-5 anchor of sensible dependency-aware grouping. It fell short of level 8 because its 'milestone' language was largely repeated boilerplate rather than an adaptive map, its done-checks were loose pass-count readings rather than pre-planned test-group targets, and shared primitives were repeatedly rebuilt (plus a self-inflicted API-overwrite crisis) rather than built once. This places it solidly at 5, not higher.

dimensions.name: Parity verification & discrepancy localization

evidence.note: Ran tests iteratively with --nocapture to surface PARITY FAILURE messages; found test-name/path mismatches and verified NOA then EDA pass before moving on — iterative group/individual verification (above anchor 3).

On BIF/EDA mismatch, localized to specific fields: minColSha=2 vs 0, node color EX-yellow vs EX-blue index, relation ordering pd,pp,gi vs gi,pd,pp — precise field-level discrepancy localization beyond 'first mismatching region'.
Inspected the harness's normalize_bif_colors/assert_parity to learn what is stripped vs compared before diffing — deliberate understanding of the comparison mechanism.
Consulted generator.log and test_manifest.toml to infer the underlying ordering rule from golden artifacts, trying to validate the true algorithm rather than blind-fitting.

Java reference absent ('No reference/ directory'; .java find failed), so no cross-check against Java behavior was possible; agent relied solely on goldens + prior knowledge — the defining element of anchor 8 is absent.

In final phase continued eyeballing goldens (grep '<node'/'<link', head of output.bif) to pinpoint drain-zone/attribute divergences; never built a novel-input or Java-vs-Rust comparison harness (no anchor-10 behavior).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs relevant test groups iteratively and inspects golden output to localize discrepancies at the specific-field/value level (minColSha, color index, relation order, grouping), and even studies the harness's normalization logic — clearly exceeding anchor 5's 'first mismatching region.' However, it never cross-checks against the Java reference (which was unavailable) to validate the underlying rule, and builds no repeatable or novel-input comparison harness, so it does not reach anchor 8 or 10. This places it at a 6: precise byte/field-level golden diffing, but comparison confined to provided goldens.

dimensions.name: Test-landscape progress tracking

evidence.note: Runs default_tests suite and records '12 of 85 tests pass', enumerating which pipeline stages work (SIF/layout/NOA) vs remaining stub modules — an early, mostly-accurate tally.
Tracks '14 of 85 default tests pass' and lists remaining categories (CLI handlers, runners helpers, edge-layout/BIF), showing an area-level done/remaining picture.

Detects a regression/state problem: triangle EDA shows OLD algorithm output, reasoning the round-robin default.rs was overwritten or didn't compile — genuine monitoring of the passing area's stability.
Terminal buffering leaves the agent unsure whether tests completed; it loses track of live test state and issues repeated C-c / restart commands.

Circular debugging: repeatedly re-runs sif_triangle EDA/BIF and re-attempts drain-zone/color fixes without recognizing this single bug is consuming disproportionate cycles or stepping back to re-diagnose.
Multiple premature 'Mark task complete' submissions while 43/259 tests pass, showing the progress model is tracked numerically but not always coherently acted upon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it periodically runs the workspace suite, keeps mostly-accurate passing/failing tallies across default and parity subsets, breaks remaining work into categories, and even catches one regression (round-robin overwrite). But it falls short of level 8 because it does not recognize when a single bug consumes disproportionate cycles — it visibly thrashes on the triangle BIF drain-zone case (steps 305-316) and rationalizes rather than re-diagnosing, and it loses track of test state under terminal buffering while repeatedly declaring completion prematurely. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Model-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: On persistent triangle-EDA failure the agent revised its mental model of edge layout through several hypotheses (all-regulars-then-shadows → round-robin → global shadow queue) and decisively restructured default.rs rather than hardcoding; this is genuine model-correction on a falsified assumption.

For multi_relation relation-ordering mismatch it enumerated multiple hypotheses (first-appearance in SIF, reverse-alphabetical, file position) testing why its alphabetical model diverged — hypothesis-forming, but never resolved.

For BIF it patched magic constants straight at the visible golden (node color EX-blue index 12, minColSha=0), i.e. surface tweaking toward one golden instead of deriving the drain-zone algorithm — the falsification-blind failure mode.

Repeatedly attributes remaining failures to 'requires Java reference' and finally resigns ('I'll submit'), rather than treating the mismatches as evidence to keep correcting the model via golden re-analysis.
Reference source absent, so all correction had to be grounded in golden re-analysis; the agent did revisit goldens for edge layout but leaned on excuses for BIF/multi_relation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly forms new hypotheses and tests them when fixes fail, and in the edge-layout case treats a persistent mismatch as evidence its model is wrong and restructures decisively (anchor 8 for that one component). But across the broader trajectory it falls into golden-directed patching of magic numbers (BIF colors/drain zones), leaves multi_relation ordering unresolved, and repeatedly attributes failure to the missing reference and gives up. This blend of occasional source(golden)-grounded correction with substantial surface tweaking and resignation matches anchor 5 with a slight lean toward 6.

dimensions.name: Faithful implementation vs golden overfitting

evidence.note: Agent discovered no Java reference exists and chose to reverse-engineer algorithms from golden files — high overfitting risk, yet it consistently framed the goal as deriving the underlying rule.

Reverse-engineered the edge-layout algorithm into a general 'global shadow queue' rule from simple goldens (triangle, single_edge) and applied it uniformly, rather than special-casing outputs per test.

When multi_relation EDA ordering failed, it kept trying to derive the general relation-ordering rule (first appearance vs alphabetical vs file position) instead of hardcoding the golden's exact sequence.

Hardcoded the exact 31/32-color golden palette into color.rs — the one shortcut, but a fixed palette is a legitimate BioFabric constant (and later found colors are normalized away in comparison), so not genuine output overfitting.

At the end, with 43/259 passing, it never resorted to hardcoding outputs or matching on test names to inflate the visible pass count; it kept attributing failures to incompletely-derived general algorithms (drain zones, multi-relation).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently implemented real, general logic and explicitly tried to derive the underlying Java algorithm from golden samples rather than hardcoding outputs or pattern-matching on test inputs — placing it well above the 3-5 band, with essentially no non-generalizing shortcuts (the lone hardcoded color palette is a legitimate program constant). It falls short of the level-8/10 anchors because it never explicitly acknowledged the held-out suite as a driver of its decisions and never deliberately stress-tested input-agnosticism; its generalization was implicit in intent rather than validated by construction. This lands at a 7.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon software port: reimplement a large Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library + CLI, achieving byte-level parity with the Java reference across visible AND held-out test suites. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java algorithms (node/edge ordering, layout, output formatting) where any subtle tie-break or byte differs, and from a fixed public API skeleton with many todo!() stubs. This warrants heavy, sustained meta-work: deep source-tracing of the reference, careful sequencing of dependent components, verification that localizes byte discrepancies, and disciplined correction rather than guess-and-check against goldens.

dimensions.name: Reference-source reverse engineering
dimensions.description: Reading and tracing the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source to understand the exact algorithms and output formats before/while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible to hit by guessing from signatures and test names; the only ground truth for ordering, tie-breaks, and formatting lives in the Java source, so accurate understanding of it gates every deliverable.

anchors.0: Implements against skeleton signatures / test names / golden fragments without opening the Java reference at all.
anchors.3: Skims a Java file once for the feature being coded; relies mostly on guessing output shape from goldens.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each feature before implementing it, extracting the core algorithm correctly for the common case.
anchors.8: Systematically maps Java classes to Rust modules, traces the exact code paths that emit output, and identifies ordering/tie-break/formatting rules (not just the happy path) directly from source.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise source archaeology: pins down subtle determinants of byte output (iteration order, sort stability, numeric/string formatting, edge cases in the alignment plugin), cross-references call sites, and re-consults the source as new discrepancies reveal gaps in understanding.

dimensions.name: Component sequencing & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into ordered sub-goals (parsing, core model, layout, ordering, CLI, alignment) with explicit done-checks, respecting dependencies.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many interdependent components feed the same outputs; building layout before a correct model, or CLI before core, wastes effort and produces cascading parity failures, so ordered milestones with clear completion signals sustain progress.

anchors.0: Attacks stubs in arbitrary order with no visible plan; jumps between unrelated components.
anchors.3: Loosely goes test-by-test with no dependency reasoning; foundations and dependents interleaved haphazardly.
anchors.5: Groups work sensibly (e.g., parsing/model first, then layout, then CLI) and finishes coherent chunks before moving on.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones tied to concrete done-checks (specific test groups green), sequenced so each unblocks the next and shared primitives are built once.
anchors.10: Clear dependency-aware milestone hierarchy that anticipates which components share output-formatting logic, sequences the hardest parity-critical pieces early, and adjusts the milestone map as the true structure of the Java code emerges.

dimensions.name: Parity verification & discrepancy localization
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing how to confirm byte-level correctness — diffing against goldens/Java, localizing where output first diverges — beyond just running the given tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite means passing visible goldens is necessary but insufficient; the agent needs verification that isolates the exact source of a byte mismatch and confirms the true algorithm, not just green visible tests.

anchors.0: Assumes code is correct; rarely runs the suite; no diffing when output mismatches.
anchors.3: Runs provided tests and eyeballs pass/fail, but on a mismatch retries blindly without pinpointing where bytes diverge.
anchors.5: Runs the relevant test groups iteratively and inspects diff output to find the first mismatching region before fixing.
anchors.8: Byte-level diffing to localize discrepancies precisely, and cross-checks behavior against the Java reference (or its expected output) rather than only the golden, to validate the underlying rule.
anchors.10: Builds/uses a repeatable comparison harness (e.g., generating novel inputs and comparing Rust vs Java behavior) to guard against held-out failures, systematically verifying edge cases and formatting invariants the visible goldens don't cover.

dimensions.name: Test-landscape progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate view of which test groups pass/remain across the whole suite and detecting stuck/circular debugging.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many tests and a stubborn class of byte-parity bugs, losing track of done-vs-remaining or looping on one failing case wastes the horizon and risks regressions in already-passing areas.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; unaware how many tests pass or what's left.
anchors.3: Occasional full runs but no running model of remaining work; surprised by regressions.
anchors.5: Periodically runs the workspace suite and keeps a rough, mostly-accurate tally of passing vs failing groups.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate done/remaining picture across parity/analysis/CLI suites, watches for regressions in passing areas, and recognizes when a single bug is consuming disproportionate cycles.
anchors.10: Continuously calibrated progress model across the horizon; explicitly detects thrashing/circular fixes on a stubborn parity bug and steps back to re-diagnose rather than re-attempting variations.

dimensions.name: Model-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the mental model / approach when a parity result contradicts an assumed Java behavior, rather than tweaking blindly toward the golden.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Parity failures usually mean the agent's model of the Java algorithm is wrong; the productive response is to return to the source and correct the model, not to patch outputs until a specific golden matches (which fails held-out cases).

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach or hardcodes toward the golden regardless of why it diverged.
anchors.3: Makes surface tweaks in response to failures without questioning whether the underlying algorithm model is wrong.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, forms a new hypothesis and tests it, occasionally revisiting the source.
anchors.8: Treats a persistent mismatch as evidence the model is wrong, returns to the Java source to correct it, and updates related code consistently.
anchors.10: Recognizes when a whole component's approach is mis-derived (e.g., wrong layout/ordering algorithm) and restructures decisively, abandoning guess-and-check loops in favor of source-grounded correction that also fixes latent held-out cases.

dimensions.name: Faithful implementation vs golden overfitting
dimensions.description: Strategically choosing to implement the true algorithm (so held-out networks pass) rather than special-casing or hardcoding to satisfy visible goldens.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly warns of a held-out suite and demands a faithful rewrite; an agent that optimizes only for visible goldens will silently fail hidden cases, so the meta-decision to generalize is itself a distinct quality signal.

anchors.0: Hardcodes outputs or pattern-matches on known test inputs to force visible goldens green.
anchors.3: Frequently special-cases to pass a specific golden without deriving the general rule.
anchors.5: Generally implements real logic, with occasional shortcuts that would not generalize.
anchors.8: Consistently implements the general algorithm from the source, explicitly avoiding golden-specific shortcuts, aware that held-out inputs must also pass.
anchors.10: Treats the visible goldens as samples of a general contract, deliberately validating that the implementation is input-agnostic and stress-testing generality, so held-out networks are covered by construction.
